approvedDesign.title: Overrun: hostile and patrol groups are fielded as if the level expected one more grade (x2.2 bodies, in packs, each body 2.25 levels weaker per added grade), and kill gems follow the fielded level
approvedDesign.problem: The board offers Infested ("A third of the cast comes one grade up", x1.35) and the cast is exactly as written (missiontypes.js:827). Read literally, one grade is a poor unit: a body one grade up is x3.8, x4.8 or x1.5 in hp x damage x speed depending on the grade, so no single multiplier prices it. The game already has the rule for a place that is overrun: swarm() (missiontypes.js:310) turns every grade a group sits below what its level expects (NATIVE, :286) into x2.2 bodies fielded 4.5 levels lower, placed in packs, with a brief tag (a pack / a swarm / a tide) and a note that the ground decides how many reach the squad at once (sortie.js briefBox, combat.js frontage, the tactics stand play). A contract that is not already below its level's grade never uses it. This design raises the expected grade by one for the contract. It needs one change outside the twist: gem drops per kill do not depend on the level the body was fielded at (missions.js:243), so more bodies means more gems, and the surplus is larger than the contract fee (measured below).
evidence: missiontypes.js:286-318: NATIVE(lv) is 0 below level 6, 1 from 6, 2 from 12, 3 from 17; HORDE_SWELL 2.2, HORDE_STEP 4.5, HORDE_CAP 40 (HORDE_CAP_PER 20 for per groups), HORDE_PACK [0, 5, 9, 14]; swarm(group, lv) computes gap = min(3, NATIVE(lv) - GRADES.indexOf(group.grade)) and returns the group unchanged when gap < 1 or the count would not rise.

missiontypes.js:945-952 roll() applies swarm before spec.terms, so terms already read the swollen counts; spec.cast and spec.terms draw no random numbers, so rollTwists can move above the cast at the same RNG position (seeded comparison over 600 rolls: 499 identical, 89 differ only where Infested or Reinforcements was rolled, 12 only on duel / dungeon / escort, whose legal pool changed).

bestiary.js:212 and sortie.js briefBox (:1045) already print the horde tag and the ground note; mapgen.js packs() places a swarmed group in packs; field.js:84 SWARMED and makeActor give swarmed bodies reduced hp and power; sortie.js fighterFor spawns them at mission level + levelOffset, clamped to level 1.

missions.js:243 rollLoot: gems per kill = (2 + 1.5 x mission.level) x tier reward x (0.8 to 1.2), whatever level the body was fielded at; combat.js:619 pushes { def, mods, killer } for each kill, and the fielded level is t.level on the dead combatant (combat.js:120).
field.js:1582 escalate() respawns 50% of g.count of every hostile and patrol group: the fielded count, swollen or not.
quests.js:116 rolls trial contracts through MT.roll with no trial flag (see reinforcements-a); a solo trial against a pack of 22 has no frontage advantage.

Rolled casts (arr3/swellstats.js, 40 rolls per type per level, 15 types), bodies per contract, written -> with Infested: level 1: 8.5 -> 16.4; 3: 11.1 -> 21.2; 5: 13.5 -> 25.0; 6: 27.4 -> 44.2; 10: 35.6 -> 48.8; 14: 52.9 -> 70.7; 18: 74.3 -> 79.1. Share of groups that change: 50% at levels 1-5, 92% at 6, 61% at 12-16, 36% at 18, 28% at 20. Share already at the cap: 0% at levels 1-5, 15% at 10, 39% at 12-16, 66-73% at 18-20. At levels 18-20, 27-35% of contracts have no group that can swell.

Measured on test/sortie.harness.js (combat-backed; gearless 3-5 star random-class squads of 4; levels 1-8, 75 contracts per level; 15 types, no duel; paired seeds). With the existing swarm calibration (every added grade 4.5 levels weaker), 600 paired contracts: wins 35.7 -> 29.2%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.78, fee 78.5 -> 66.1, loot 53.7 -> 57.9, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.5, fights 6.1 -> 5.9. The twist lowers deaths (0.97 -> 0.78) and wins (35.7% -> 29.2%): contracts that end with "they ran from a fight they were losing" go from 48% to 56%, wipes from 13% to 11%. Gem drops without the rollLoot change: wins 35.7 -> 29.5%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.78, fee 78.5 -> 67.2, loot 73.2 -> 121.2, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.5, fights 6.1 -> 5.9.

With the added grade 2.25 levels weaker instead of 4.5 (the design below), 600 paired contracts against the same base with the rollLoot change: wins 35.7 -> 26.3%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.99, fee per attempt 78.5 -> 56.4, loot per attempt 53.7 -> 54.6, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.4, fights 6.1 -> 5.8, contracts with a death 41.2% -> 39.7%. By level: L1-3 wins 68>50% deaths 0.40>0.39; L4-5 wins 28>19% deaths 1.02>0.97; L6-8 wins 9>8% deaths 1.51>1.60. Contract endings, base / this design: won 35% / 26%, ran from a fight 48% / 55%, squad down 13% / 15%. A quarter step (1 level weaker per added grade) gives wins 24.8% and deaths 1.08, price 1.64.

Loot change alone on the base contracts (15 types, levels 1-8, no twist; existing swarms are the level 6-8 part): wins 35.7 -> 35.7%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.97, fee 78.5 -> 78.5, loot 73.2 -> 53.7, hostiles 19.3 -> 19.3, fights 6.1 -> 6.1. Level 12-18 probe (5 types, 60 paired contracts, gearless squads): hostiles per contract 60.2 -> 73.0, Node CPU per contract 2602 -> 2693 ms, 7% of rolls had no group that could swell and dropped the tag.
approvedDesign.change:
MODS (the table row, data only): infested: { label: 'Infested', weight: 10, reward: 1.40, not: ['duel'], trial: false, mods: { swell: { grades: 1, step: 0.5 } } }. MT.modsOf folds swell by summing grades (capped at 2); step belongs to the one twist that sets it. The desc is generated from the rolled cast by MOD_TEXT.swell(value, mission): "Hostile and patrol groups are fielded as if the level expected 1 more grade than it does: x2.2 bodies per grade, in packs of 5, 9 or 14, each body 4.5 levels weaker per grade the level expects and 2.25 per grade this adds; a group at 40 bodies (20 per wave) is unchanged. On this paper: Water Slime x10 -> x22; Cave Spider x1 (unchanged). Gems per kill follow the level the body is fielded at." The counts follow the contract's intel (Bestiary.countText).

CONSUMERS.
(1) missiontypes.js. swarm(group, lv, bonus = 0, step = 1): gap = min(3, NATIVE(lv) + bonus - GRADES.indexOf(group.grade)); the level offset uses gapNat + (gap - gapNat) x step grades of HORDE_STEP, where gapNat is the gap without the bonus. New swell(group, lv, value) returns the inflated group only when it has more bodies than the plain swarm, and records swollenFrom: plain.count on it (a group already at the cap would otherwise get a deeper offset for the same count). roll() moves 'const tw' above the cast at the same RNG position, builds the cast from the written groups with swell() when mods.swell is set, and drops 'infested' from tw when no group changed (levels 18+: 27-35% of contracts), so the tag is never carried without an effect. Terms read the larger counts, as they do for any swarm. MT.current(m) (u-honesty) also rejects a mission with the id whose groups carry no swollenFrom. rollTwists(typeId, level, max, { trial }) and quests.js:116 as in reinforcements-a.
(2) combat.js:619: the kill record gets level: t.level. missions.js rollLoot (:243): the gem term uses Math.min(mission.level, kill.level || mission.level), so a body fielded below the mission level pays for the level it was fielded at, and a grade-bumped body (GRADE_BUMP) does not pay more than it did. This reprices every existing swarm contract (level 6 and up, where basic groups are below their level's grade). Measured with no twist, over 15 types and levels 1-8: wins 35.7 -> 35.7%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.97, fee 78.5 -> 78.5, loot 73.2 -> 53.7, hostiles 19.3 -> 19.3, fights 6.1 -> 6.1; levels 6-8 alone: loot 101 -> 49 gems per attempt.
(3) MOD_TEXT.swell as above. The Hardcore line gains "the escalation respawn adds 50% of the fielded count of each hostile and patrol group, swollen or not" (field.js:1582), which is already true of every swarm.
(4) bestiary.js brief(): the row copies swollenFrom, and sortie.js briefBox prints "(was x10)" beside the existing horde tag. Nothing else: castLevel, noteSighting, fighterFor, the pack placement, the plain-model hp and power and the tactics stand play are the existing swarm path.
(5) test/contracts.js: per group, count >= the roll without the twist; capped groups unchanged; terms equal the terms read off the swollen cast; a level-3 extermination group of 10 basic becomes 22 at -2 levels in packs of 5 and a veteran group of 1 is unchanged; at level 20 with every group capped the twist is dropped and reward is 1; rollLoot pays (2 + 1.5 x 1) for a body fielded at level 1 under a level-8 mission. test/sortie.harness.js TWISTS=none|id and test/twistprice.js as in reinforcements-a.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag "Infested x1.40" with the generated desc and the factor line; the expect line shows the swollen rows ("Water Slime lvl 1 x22"); the brief shows the existing horde tag and the ground note. Map: packs of small bodies standing together (mapgen packs) and the existing log text for ground ("meet ... in a doorway") on each fight. The decision the card supports is the ground: the contract names its map, and MAPS[...].cover is the number behind it.

REWARD x1.40. Same rule and tool as reinforcements-a: pay0 + loot0 - 100 x dead0 = m x pay1 + loot1 - 100 x dead1, against the base with the rollLoot change. Inputs (600 paired contracts): wins 35.7 -> 26.3%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.99, fee per attempt 78.5 -> 56.4, loot per attempt 53.7 -> 54.6: m = 1.40, rounded to 1.40. With the death price at 50 / 150 / 200 gems: 1.39 / 1.42 / 1.43. The price is mostly the lost fee (wins fall 9.3 points), not deaths, which stay level; wound downtime is not in it (loop-wounds not built). The player's check: the card title itemises the factor, the brief shows each swollen row with its original count, the kill gems follow the level printed on the row, and the tag tooltip shows their own record.

FREQUENCY. weight 10 (unchanged), not duel. Per contract under u-honesty's draw rule with all nine rows live: 2.8% at level 1, 4.3% at 5, 6.2% at 10, 8.2% at 15, 10.4% at 20 (original row 3.4 / 5.1 / 7.5 / 10.0 / 12.6% under today's rule); at levels 18-20 the inert guard removes 27-35% of the rolls, so the effective rate there is about 7-8%. P(at least one on a board of 5): 13% at level 1, 20% at 5, 28% at 10.
approvedDesign.playerEffect: The decision is the ground and the squad. The paper names the map and states how many bodies come (17.9 written, 30.0 with the twist, per contract); on open ground a pack of 22 reaches the squad together, in a doorway it reaches two at a time, so a player compares the contract's map cover and the squad's frontage tools (a line-holder, area damage) before launch, and the existing stand play (tactics.js) acts on it during the run. Measured effect: 9.3 fewer wins per 100 contracts, deaths level (0.97 -> 0.99), more hostiles (19.3 -> 31.4) and more wounded survivors (25.6% -> 30.5% of survivors under 40% HP at their lowest; contracts with one 54.2% -> 61.2%). Gems come from kills, valued by the level the body is fielded at.
approvedDesign.secondOrder: Wounds: 25.6% -> 30.5% of survivors under 40% HP at their lowest (the loop-wounds trigger), contracts with such a survivor 54.2% -> 61.2%: the cost of this twist is downtime. Permadeath: contracts with a death 41.2% -> 39.7%, so it neither adds nor prevents deaths at this step; at the existing calibration (4.5 levels weaker) it prevents them (41.2% -> 33.2% of contracts, m = 0.83), which would make it a favourable complication. Retreat (loop-retreat): wins fall because the squad breaks off more often (48% -> 55% of contracts end in a run from a fight it was losing), so the contract is lost without a death; the retreat order is unchanged. Debrief: fights per contract 6.1 -> 5.8 while bodies per contract rise, so casts are spent in fewer, larger fights. Loot: with the rollLoot change drops are 53.7 -> 54.6 gems per attempt; without it they would be +66% (wins 35.7 -> 29.5%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.78, fee 78.5 -> 67.2, loot 73.2 -> 121.2, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.5, fights 6.1 -> 5.9). Existing swarm contracts: gem drops fall (wins 35.7 -> 35.7%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.97, fee 78.5 -> 78.5, loot 73.2 -> 53.7, hostiles 19.3 -> 19.3, fights 6.1 -> 6.1); the contract fee is unchanged. Hardcore: escalation respawns 50% of the swollen count, so Infested + Hardcore escalates harder (a 22-body group adds 11); rare (together on about 0.06% of level-1 and 0.6% of level-20 contracts) and now stated in the Hardcore text. Night: no interaction. No resupply: attrition over more, smaller fights is where the two stack, and it is not measured.
approvedDesign.risks: Build after u-honesty. Two parts, one unit: without the rollLoot change this twist adds +66% gem drops (wins 35.7 -> 29.5%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.78, fee 78.5 -> 67.2, loot 73.2 -> 121.2, hostiles 19.3 -> 31.5, fights 6.1 -> 5.9), larger than the fee, and no sane multiplier fixes that; if the rollLoot change is declined, do not build the twist. The rollLoot change is an economy change for every existing swarm contract (level 6 and up): gem drops there fall by roughly half (wins 35.7 -> 35.7%, deaths 0.97 -> 0.97, fee 78.5 -> 78.5, loot 73.2 -> 53.7, hostiles 19.3 -> 19.3, fights 6.1 -> 6.1; levels 6-8 alone: loot 101 -> 49 gems per attempt). If the user wants existing swarm pay left alone, the fallback is a per-group field lootLevel set only by swell() (one field, one branch in rollLoot) at the cost of two payout rules. Harness: gearless squads (absolute deaths are upper bounds), levels 1-8; levels 12-18 were measured for body counts and run time only (gearless squads win none of them). The step (0.5) is a dial chosen on the harness: at 1.0 the twist lowers deaths (m = 0.83), at 0.25 it costs 10.9 win points for m = 1.64; the price is mostly lost fee. Low levels: bodies are fielded at max(1, level - offset), so at levels 1-3 the swollen bodies are at or near level 1 (L1-3 wins 68>50% deaths 0.40>0.39), a larger win-rate drop than at 6-8. Frame time in the browser at 40+ hostiles is not measured (overseer check); Node CPU per contract rose 1839 -> 2165 ms on levels 1-8 and 2602 -> 2693 ms at levels 12-18. Per type, wins and deaths move in both directions (assassination 33>25% 2.30>2.35; capture 43>40% 1.57>1.45; dungeon 18>10% 1.63>1.82; escort 90>98% 0.57>0.33; expedition 55>45% 0.65>0.30; extermination 48>43% 0.60>0.47; hold 30>8% 0.10>0.03; pursuit 38>35% 0.97>0.30; raid 25>5% 1.25>1.38; recon 38>43% 0.75>0.45; rescue 40>13% 0.60>0.93; retrieval 30>43% 0.90>0.10; sabotage 20>3% 1.10>0.63; siege 3>5% 1.45>1.07; survival 28>25% 0.10>0.07); the multiplier is an average.
approvedDesign.response:
Design attack. (1) "Strictly favourable, a bonus that reads as a complication": confirmed and worse than stated. At the existing swarm calibration the twist lowers deaths (0.97 -> 0.78) and the drop surplus is +66%. Two changes: the added grade is 2.25 levels weaker instead of 4.5 (deaths level, wins -9.3 points, m = 1.40), and kill gems follow the fielded level so the surplus is gone; both are measured above. (2) "Wounds are a downtime tax paid in gems": stated with the proxy; wound downtime is not in the price until loop-wounds exists. (3) "Level 12+ basic groups are at the cap": measured as rolled casts and as run time, and the inert guard drops the tag where nothing swells. (4) Hardcore re-spawn: stated in the Hardcore text. (5) Desc example wrong for the level (a veteran group of 5 does not swell at level 3): confirmed; the desc is now generated from the rolled cast. (6) Trials: trial: false with the shared plumbing. Demands: loot surplus removed inside the proposal (done, measured, with its side effect on existing swarms stated), desc generated (done), a level 12-18 cell (done for bodies and run time; outcomes need geared squads), trial: false, Hardcore line (done).
Engineering attack. Surplus: as above. Level 12+ inertness: guarded. Hostiles per run and frame time: Node CPU and hostile counts reported, browser frame time left to the overseer. Hardcore: stated. u-honesty ordering: stated. Positive levelOffset: not used by this design (infested-a, which needed it, is dropped).

verdicts.attack: At x1.00 it pays about +18% expected gems per attempt because kill drops use the mission level, not the body's (missions.js:242), so a player who reads the brief prefers Infested contracts: a complication that is a bonus. Deaths are flat and wounds rise (14.4% to 18.3% of survivors), so under u-wounds it is a downtime tax paid in gems. Above level 12 basic groups already sit at HORDE_CAP 40, so only veteran and elite groups swell; unmeasured. Infested with Hardcore re-spawns 50% of the swollen count (field.js:1557). The generated desc example is wrong for the level it implies: veterans swell only from level 6 (NATIVE 1 + bonus 1 against GRADES index 1), so a paper with '10 to 22 basic' at level 3 shows '5 veteran' unchanged, not '5 to 11'. Trials are not excluded.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: NATIVE(lv) 0/1/2/3 at 1/6/12/17, HORDE_SWELL 2.2, HORDE_STEP 4.5, HORDE_CAP 40, HORDE_CAP_PER 20, HORDE_PACK [0,5,9,14], swarm() returning the group unchanged when gap < 1 or count does not rise (missiontypes.js:286-318); roll() swarms before terms :945-952; brief horde tag sortie.js:995 and the ground note :1010-1014; packs placement mapgen.js:259-268 and :333-334; SWARMED and makeActor hp/power field.js:84, 1682-1683; rollLoot missions.js:238-243; duel bouts are veteran groups per bout :734. Scratchpad final2.txt and final-n100: inf_h1 62.1%/0.253 (n=1500) matches exactly.
verdicts.demand: Remove the surplus inside the proposal: either rollLoot takes the body's fielded level (measured on this harness) or the row's reward is set so income per attempt is neutral and the card says 'paid in drops' with the computed figure. Correct the desc example or generate it from the real cast. Measure one level 12-18 cell. Add trial: false. Add one line to the Hardcore MOD_TEXT: escalation re-spawns 50% of the fielded count, swollen or not.

verdicts.attack: At multiplier 1.00 the builder's own numbers give expected income per attempt about 18% above the base (drops 54.1 to 96.3 gems per run, fee 121.1 to 109.6), because rollLoot (missions.js:238-242) pays (2 + 1.5 x level) per kill regardless of the body's fielded level. A complication that is strictly favourable inverts the honesty premise: players take every Infested contract and the tag reads as a bonus. The builder names the fix (scale drops by fielded level) and declines to own it. Above level 12 basic groups sit at HORDE_CAP 40 (missiontypes.js:295), so the row is inert for them and only veteran/elite groups swell; not measured (harness reaches level 8). Hostiles per run rise 13 to 24 (35 at level 8), the only perf cost of the twelve that is measured, and not measured in the browser. Hardcore's escalate() respawns 50% of the swollen count (field.js:1559), admitted and rare.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: NATIVE :286 (0 below 6, 1 from 6, 2 from 12, 3 from 17), HORDE_SWELL 2.2, HORDE_STEP 4.5, HORDE_CAP 40, HORDE_CAP_PER 20, HORDE_PACK [0,5,9,14]; swarm() :310-318 with gap = min(3, NATIVE - grade index) and the count-must-rise guard; roll() :945 applies swarm before terms :952; brief horde tag at sortie.js:995 and the ground note :1010-1014; packs() :259; SWARMED :84; rollLoot :238-253 uses mission.level only; Math.round(4.5) = 5 so a 10-body basic at level 3 with bonus 1 becomes 22 at -5 in packs of 5 as claimed. Scratchpad proj2 swarm(group, lv, bonus) and the swell comparison match. results/final-n100 inf_h1: 62.1% / 0.253 / 14.1% (exact); hi1.txt 55.0% / 0.403 / hostiles 34.9 (exact); loot2.txt wins 63.3% (exact).
verdicts.demand: After u-honesty. Decide the surplus before it ships: either a separate approved change to rollLoot (gems scaled by the body's fielded level, which changes every existing horde contract) or a reward below 1.00 printed on the card as the drop-share line the builder already drafts. Measure hostiles per run and frame time in the browser at level 8, and the level 12+ inertness on test/sortie.harness.js. The overseer approves at most one of infested-a and infested-b; this is the lower-death, single-axis one, and the only one of the pair without a conventional price.

sharedRules: Shared rules the user approved for every complication: (1) one price rule: the multiplier keeps expected gems per attempt equal, counting a death at PULL_COST (100 gems), R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x 100 / (p1 x W0), rounded up to the next 0.05; (2) every number is re-measured on test/sortie.harness.js (add TWISTS=, GEAR=1 options if missing), not on a private runner; (3) at most one body-adding complication per contract (reinforcements, hunted, trap, turncoat, infested) until pairs are measured; (4) log lines state what spawned, where, at what distance and which term changed, in the engineering register; (5) trial: false on every row that adds bodies, threaded through quests.js.

conflicts: Three pricing conventions for the same quantity. Terrain prices a death at PULL_COST 100 gems and rounds up to 0.05; arrivals prices it at 200 gems plus kill drops; pursuit uses the relative rise in deaths with no formula. Same-sized effects get different multipliers: hunted-a +0.11 deaths per run -> x1.4, reinforcements-a +0.16 -> x1.25, infested-a +0.14 -> x1.50, trap-a +0.012 -> x1.15, storm-a +0.03 -> x1.05. None of the multipliers is derivable by the player from anything on screen (numbers-must-be-traceable); the per-twist record all three propose as the check is specified three ways (gs.field.twists { sent, won, dead } in terrain and arrivals; 'u-ledger can add' in pursuit) and u-ledger part A defines only gs.field.types. One owner, one R stated as data, one record shape.

Exit-route stacking. reinforcements-a (column from the entry 45 s after contact), hunted-a and hunted-b (a body trailing the squad), trap-a (a mark at the way home) and turncoat-a (the ward at the far end) all add bodies to the walk out, where the pursuit lens measured most deaths already occur. rollTwists allows two twists per contract (missiontypes.js:863, max 2) and no proposal measured any pair; the multipliers multiply (1.25 x 1.4 = 1.75) while the deaths very likely compound. Hardcore pairs are treated four different ways (trap-a skips once escalated, reinforcements-a skips arrival groups in the escalation re-spawn, infested-b doubles the escalation re-spawn through the swollen count, storms scale the escape window) and none is measured.

hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same mechanism (a hostile group released behind the squad that reaches it on the way out); the pursuit builder says approve one. hunted-a's dominant effect (the squad bumps into a trailing elite) is the same mechanism again with one body.

Every proposal depends on u-honesty (MT.modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, TWIST_FULL, MT.factors, MT.payout), none of which exists in the code (grep finds no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, TWIST_FULL or MT.current in *.js). The mods fold table would carry about 15 keys with three fold semantics (multiply: move, damage, regen, sight; union/concat: noReach, status, arrivals; largest: promote; sum: swell; first: ambush, pit; plus follower/pack/turn/informant) and the pursuit rows add a cast: (lv) => [...] function on the TWISTS row that must never reach a saved mission. 'A twist is a table row plus one consumer' becomes a dispatch table; the fold rules need one owner and one test.

Field flags for 'a hostile that moves on its own trigger' are named four ways: march (reinforcements-a), stance 'trail' / 'pack' plus follows (hunted-a/b), spotted preset true (hunted), spottedAt (reinforcements-b); each adds ACTOR_KEYS entries and a chooseGoals branch. trapTick/ringTile are claimed by trap-a and trap-b and offered to Reinforcements. u-retreat's contacted() is edited by trap-a (adds s.trapped) and paralleled by reinforcements-a's contactAt; one definition of contact must serve the button, the column clock and the trap.

Frequency figures use different rules: terrain and pursuit quote u-honesty's odds x weight / 66; arrivals quotes today's rule with nine rows. With all rows live the legal pool exceeds 66 on every type (73 to 102 by weights proposed), so the honesty promise 'others unchanged until the weights sum to 66' fails slightly: by my exact two-draw calculation over the 16 types, at level 10 dry falls 6.5% to 5.9-6.1% and hardcore 5.5% to 5.0-5.2%. reinforcements-b (weight 24) and turncoat-a (weight 12) are weight hikes with no stated reason beyond compensating 'only'.

storm-a and storm-b are alternatives, but storm-b's bow rule changes every water-spell Wet outside storms (elements.js:170 is shared with spellcraft.js:54), while storm-a's lives only in combat.js; approving storm-b as written is a global balance change, approving storm-a is a twist-local special case. Both carry the same unpriced walking tax on window contracts.

Three private combat-backed runners (proto/exp/real.js, arrivals/run.js, pursuit/run.js) with three baselines (82.4%/0.10-0.115, 69.5%/0.258, 68.4%/0.251 deaths per run) that cannot be compared, while test/sortie.harness.js, the project's combat-backed harness (named in memory and in test/field.harness.js's header), was used by none; the terrain lens asks for 'a combat-backed runner in test/' that already exists.
missed: Trials. quests.js:116 rolls trial twists through MT.roll with no flag and no filter, so star trials, including the one-body solo road, draw every row. Only the pursuit lens adds trial: false, and it describes quests.js:116 as already passing trial: true, which it does not. Storm, Reinforcements (at least one extra body per written group against a single character), Infested and A trap on a solo trial are unmeasured and unexcluded.

The one-sided-fight quirk. sortie.js:158-160 gives noFightUntil = clock + 120 to every actor in a skirmish whose party or foes list is empty, so any hostile that catches a lone ward (no species, no fighter) is pacified for 120 in-game seconds. trap-a and turncoat-a both put a mark next to a ward, and nobody checked this path; it is also the reason 0 of 960 wards died, which the pursuit lens reports as a fact without the cause.

Phase 'leaving' is set both by withdraw() (field.js:383, a broken squad running) and by leave() (field.js:1875, the job done). The pursuit lens's premise that the walk out is 'the unthreatened part of a run' (76 of 100 deaths after leaving) counts post-withdrawal deaths; u-retreat's exitState reads s.withdrew and s.phase too. Any design that keys on 'the walk home' needs the two split.

The walking-speed term on window contracts. makePortal's shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1308); both storms scale only Hardcore's escape window, so escort and rescue (deadline true -> window) take the whole x0.8 tax: storm-b's own result file shows escort deaths 0.07 to 0.20-0.23 per run, unreported, and storm-a's shows rescue 0.07 to 0.12 from the move term alone.

Loadouts are planned once against a pseudoZone of species at mission level (missions.js:97-100 samples every species at mission.level; sortie.js:112 keys the cache by species count). infested-a's promoted third is fielded at level + 3 but planned against at mission level; storm-a/b and reinforcements-a patch the cache key, infested-a does not. missionProfile needs the fielded level per body or the brilliant-mind planning advantage the storm proposals claim does not exist for promoted casts.

Permadeath value. The user rates anything that prevents a death far above damage; all twelve proposals add deaths (+0.012 to +0.235 per run) and none adds a lever that prevents one. The only readable 'leave now' signals are reinforcements-a's countdown and hunted-a's HP gate. A complication whose counterplay is a death-prevention action (a window in which the retreat order is free again, a spotter kill that cancels an arrival the squad can see) would fit the stated values; none was proposed.

Register. Proposed log lines include 'The paper was wrong: <label> is here for them', 'The floor gives way', 'the pack closes in', 'come out of the dark', 'The informant left': narrative, not the mechanic and the number (ui-prose-engineer-style). Every new line should read like the existing 'Complications: Storm' and 'wave 2 of 4' lines: what spawned, where, at what distance, and which term changed.

Save compatibility of board offers. A held board offer or saved run rolled before the build carries a twist id whose row now has mods or a cast function; the pursuit lens stales such offers through MT.current, the arrivals lens does not (a saved 'reinforcements' contract pays x1.25 with no column until the board rerolls), and the terrain lens derives mods from mission.twists so old runs change behaviour mid-run on reload. One rule for 'an offer rolled under an older table' is needed across all rows.

No proposal measured on a real save with gear and potions (all say so) or with the two-twist pairs the board can roll; and no proposal gives the overseer a repeatable command in test/ that reproduces its headline numbers, which test/sortie.harness.js's OUT/diff mode already supports.

conflicts: Alternatives on one row: storm-a/storm-b, trap-a/trap-b, reinforcements-a/reinforcements-b, infested-a/infested-b, hunted-a/hunted-b each re-add the same TWISTS id with different mods keys, MOD_TEXT lines, weights and only/not lists; at most one per row can land, and the arrivals lens did not say so for its two pairs.

Three incompatible price rules. Terrain: R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x PULL_COST(100) / (p1 x W0), no drops. Arrivals: m = (W0 F0 + L0 + 200 dd - L1) / (W1 F1), a death costs 200 and kill drops count. Pursuit: the measured relative rise in deaths, no formula. On the same inputs hunted-a is 1.19 (terrain rule), 1.24 (arrivals rule) or 1.4 (as proposed); turncoat-a at levels 1-4 is about 1.08 against 1.5; infested-a is 1.31 against 1.50; storm-a is 1.05 against about 1.10. u-honesty's MT.factors prints these multipliers side by side on one card, so the six rows must be priced by one rule.

Weight budget. u-honesty's draw rule is odds x min(1, poolWeight / TWIST_FULL) with TWIST_FULL = 66 and the promise that adding rows leaves the others unchanged 'until the weights sum to 66'. The original nine rows sum to 84; with the A variants the per-type pool is 75-87, with the B variants 64-96 (reinforcements-b 24, infested-b 13, turncoat-a 12), so the cap binds everywhere: my simulation (60000 rolls per level) has night 7.89% to 7.51%, dry 6.49% to 6.02%, hardcore 5.67% to 5.19% at level 10 under the A weights, and each lens computed its own frequency under a different pool (pursuit: three live rows plus its own; terrain: the same; arrivals: all nine on the current rule). One owner must set TWIST_FULL to the real total or rescale the weights.

Four cue-spawn mechanisms for one idea. reinforcements-a/b: cast groups with arrive {on, delay} and a fired flag in map.spawns, march stance, contactAt/spottedAt; hunted-a/b: TEMPORAL 'trail', cued(), counters.trailed, stance trail/pack with their own chooseGoals branches and taskGoal/rally skips; trap-a: springAmbush with ringTile and a mark; all walk a new hostile group onto the map on a cue and give it a goal rule. The axes memory asks for one mechanism with data ({on, delay, from, stance}) read by one spawner and one goal branch; the pursuit lens itself says the stance code 'should land once'.
hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same effect (bodies arriving from the entry behind the squad) under two labels and two prices (x1.4 and x1.25); the pursuit lens says do not approve both.

Trial roads. hunted-a/b and turncoat-a/b add trial: false and a rollTwists filter; storm, trap, reinforcements and infested do not, so a one-body solo trial can roll Reinforcements, Infested or Storm. The claim that quests.js:116 passes trial: true is false today (mt.roll(type, { level, name }); roll() has no trial option), so whichever lands first must thread it.

u-retreat's contacted() is extended three ways: trap-a adds !!s.trapped, reinforcements-a mirrors it with s.contactAt set in look() and openSkirmish(), hunted pre-marks followers spotted to stay out of it; one definition of contact, in one place, before any of these.

MOD_TEXT shape. u-honesty specifies a static table keyed by mod; terrain and arrivals generate per-contract text (member lines, 'x bodies on this paper', species tags), so the honesty API must take (mods, mission) before these build; infested-b's and reinforcements-a's cards cannot be produced from the static table.

All three lenses say wave 1 is editing field.js, sortie.js, combat.js and missiontypes.js. Wave 1 is finished (.team-backup/r1w1, project files dated 01:xx-03:06); wave 2 started at 03:09 (.team-backup/r1w2) and holds u-honesty, u-retreat, u-wounds, u-ledger, u-readout and u-debrief, which touch every file these twelve cite. Every line number here moves before any of them builds, and none lists after: ['u-honesty', 'u-retreat'] in a form the scheduler reads.
missed: u-honesty is approved but not built: missiontypes.js has no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, MT.factors or TWIST_FULL (grep across *.js is empty) and its spec moves the six rows out of TWISTS into a comment block. All twelve proposals write MODS entries against that API and re-add rows it removes; none states the dependency as a build order, and a builder landing before it would write a second, incompatible fold.

None of the three lenses used test/sortie.harness.js (u-harness, approved and present: boots game.html's script list through test/game.boot.js and plays real Sortie launch/skip/settle with combat.js, gear, potions, Condition pools and Outfit). Each wrote a private runner that re-implements resolve(), tick() regen and nameCast with gearless parties; every absolute death rate is an upper bound by the builders' own admission, and every multiplier is priced on those numbers. The field-balance-harness memory says to quote game figures from sortie.harness.js.

Storm and the window clock: escort, assassination, rescue, pursuit, sabotage and capture carry deadline: true (missiontypes.js:409, :524, :595, :618, :640, :708), exitFor (:195) gives them the window exit, and shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1313). Walking x0.8 shortens the usable window by 20% on six types; neither storm design scales or discloses it (only Hardcore's escalate seconds are scaled).

escalate() (field.js:1557-1560) and the window-shut branch (:1373-1376) respawn 50% / 30% of every hostile and patrol spawn group with no check for deferred, at, arrive or follows, so any twist that adds a cast group gets it cloned on escalation and on every window shut. reinforcements-a skips its groups; hunted-a and hunted-b do not.

Stale offers: boards re-roll every 6 minutes (sortie.js:97) but trial offers persist per character until the star changes (quests.js:112); any twist that changes the cast at roll time (reinforcements-a/b, infested-a/b, hunted-a/b) leaves already-rolled offers carrying the tag with no bodies behind it and the multiplier still applied. Only hunted-a proposes an MT.current cast check.

describe().hostiles (missiontypes.js:1047) sums hostile+patrol+mark counts in m.cast; the card's hostile figure includes a column or follower unless excluded. hunted-a excludes follows groups; reinforcements-a/b do not.

combat.js types a spell's main strike by strikes[0].type (:303) and its splash as 'arcane' (:308); storm-a's per-type damage multiplier misses heat splash. Riposte (:215) uses the target's damageType and DoT (:593) the condition's type, so those paths are covered.

trap-a sets s.doneAt = null at the spring; verdict() (field.js:1636) withdraws with 'this is going nowhere' when !s.withdrew && !s.doneAt && s.clock >= duration x ABANDON (2.5), so a late squad is pulled out at the moment the ambush appears.

The measured cost of hunted-a, hunted-b and part of reinforcements-a is a body on the route home (hunted-a: 49 of 52 follower-fight deaths after leaving; hunted-b: 84 of 86; reinforcements-a: 26% of firings after the walk home starts), while the tooltips describe triggers (HP under 70%, commit at 60%, contact + 45 s) that the builders' own sensitivity tables show barely move the outcome. Under the traceable-numbers rule the card has to name the thing that costs.

Positive levelOffset is new to the engine: SWARMED (field.js:84) clamps it to 0.15 and feeds makeActor hp/power (:1682-1683) and every odds() call tactics makes; infested-a includes the fix, but nothing else that reads levelOffset was audited for the sign (bestiary brief, noteSighting and castLevel add it correctly; the plain harness and tactics tests assume it is negative).

Perf was measured for one proposal only (infested-b: hostiles per run 13 to 24, 35 at level 8, Node only). turncoat-b puts an actor scan under found()/known() (10 call sites in field.js, several inside per-actor filters per step); trap-b rebuilds the map mid-run; reinforcements-b scans the whole tile grid once per call. None was timed in the browser.

Evidence slips that do not change verdicts but should be corrected in the specs: terrain's fire-word class list (classes.js has mastery 'fire' in grenadier :466, artillerist :566 and kineticist :999, not arcanist or elemental_mage; the picker line must come from Classes.lexiconOf at classes.js:1818, which the proposal does name); pursuit's 'quests.js:116 passes trial: true' (it passes level and name only); the 1950-run storm figures and all trap figures are not in any results file in the scratchpad (proto/out holds storm_random.txt at n=1500 with different death rates, storm_b_wet.txt and storm_b_cands.txt), while every pursuit log and the arrivals final-n100 files reproduce the quoted numbers.
